title: Clear choking hazards from a toddler's play mat
instruction: A toddler under 3 will play on this mat. Under the US small-parts rule (a part is a choking hazard if it fits entirely inside a cylinder 31.7 mm wide and 25.4 to 57.1 mm deep), put every choking hazard in the grey bin and leave every safe toy on the mat. Then let go.
context: US law (16 CFR 1501) bans toys for children under 3 that have parts small enough to fit the small-parts test cylinder, because choking is a leading cause of injury death in young children. A robot tidying a nursery or daycare floor has to apply that rule to toys it has never seen, by size and shape, not by colour.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (bases at y = -30 right and y = +30 left): x forward, y to the left, heights above the table top. Fixed: a pale-green foam play mat, 16 (x) x 60 (y) x 1 cm, centred at x 17, y 0 (spans x 9 to 25, y -30 to +30); a grey open toy bin centred at x 34, y 0, 14 x 14 cm inside, 1 cm walls standing 7 cm tall on the table and a 1 cm floor, so the rim is 6 cm above the bin floor (outside x 26 to 42, y -8 to +8). Seven loose toys stand in one row on the mat at x 17, listed by y (centre): -24 orange rubber ball, 34 mm diameter, 23 g (safe); -10 purple wooden peg, cylinder 28 mm diameter x 60 mm tall, standing on an end, 26 g (safe); -3 red wooden cube, 20 mm, 5.6 g (hazard); +4 blue wooden block, 60 mm cube, 150 g (safe); +11 teal plastic block, 20.9 x 20.9 x 24 mm, standing on a square face, 11 g (hazard); +18 pink wooden spool, cylinder 29.6 mm diameter x 22 mm tall, standing on an end, 10.6 g (hazard); +25 steel ball, 16 mm diameter, 16.8 g (hazard). Every box toy is aligned with the table edges. Colours are distinct and do not encode hazard or safe.
scoring: Hard 0 if any toy ends with its lowest point more than 5 cm below the table top (fell off the table). Otherwise score = 0.9 x max(0, H/4 - W/3), where H = hazards (of 4) wholly inside the bin (inside the inner walls, 2 mm tolerance for a toy resting against a wall, and no part above the rim) and W = safe toys (of 3) not resting on the mat (centre not over the mat, or lowest point more than 1 cm above the mat surface, e.g. in the bin, on the table or stacked on another toy). Doing nothing scores 0; putting every toy in the bin scores 0. 1.0 requires all 4 hazards in the bin, all 3 safe toys on the mat, every toy still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) and every fingertip of both grippers at least 3 cm from every toy, all held for 1 s. A safe toy that tips over but stays on the mat still counts as on the mat.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. The mat and the bin are fixed in the simulation: in a real trial, tape the mat to the table and weight or clip down the bin. Put the seven toys back in the row positions above, the cubes and blocks square to the table edges and the peg and spool standing on an end.
fidelity: Rigid primitives with realistic sizes and masses; friction is the simulator default, not set per material. Mat and bin are fixed. Hazard or safe is decided by the real 16 CFR 1501.4 cylinder geometry, checked in code (small_parts_fit.py): every borderline toy clears the fixture by at least 1 mm either way. No flat coin-like hazard: the simulated gripper cannot pinch thin discs off a surface. Grasp, contact and release are approximate.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm went first to the safe rubber ball and knocked it off the mat, then pushed at the large block; no hazard reached the bin); scripted demo: 1.0 (4 of 4 runs)
